text:
I've marked both premises verified:
- **The SessionStart nudge works.** It reaches the model; whether you see it directly in the terminal still needs one interactive test, so the nudge also asks the model to pass it on.
- **A background subagent can run `ponytail:ponytail-audit` through the Skill tool and return its report.** Skills marked `disable-model-invocation` can't be run this way, so the config should name skills, not user-only slash commands.

**What research-queue does:** it's the bookkeeping for the background research pool. It records which jobs are queued or running and their agent ids, when each started (to spot stalled ones), and it caps parallel jobs. It holds no research: the reports already go into the change folder (`<change>/research/`). It's kept per session rather than per change only because research can also run outside any change.

Your instinct is right, and it extends to everything machine-local. Every piece of local state belongs to one change: the sessions registered to it, its review snapshot, its research queue, its implement state and its spikes. So each change gets a gitignored `.local/` inside its own folder:

```
rpir/
  config.yaml                 tracked (track: false → all of rpir/ ignored)
  research/                   standalone research + index.jsonl
  improvements/               project improvements registry
  changes/<change>/
    spec.md  plan.yaml  research/  impl-report.md  spec-retro.md  audit.md
    .local/                   always ignored: one pattern, rpir/**/.local/
      sessions                session ids registered to this change
      reviewed/               last reviewed spec + plan
      research-queue.tsv
      implement-state.json    exists only while implement is unfinished
      spikes/
```

This makes #9 simpler:
- **Finding unfinished implementations** is a single glob: `rpir/changes/*/.local/implement-state.json`.
- **Pruning** happens when the file is deleted at the end of implement.
- **Parallel runs** can't clash.

Research outside a change uses `rpir/research/.local/`.

**Migration:** a project with the old `.kentra-rpir.yaml` and `.kentra-rpir/` keeps working, and a migrate script moves it to the new layout.

input: Read ponytail-audit skill frontmatter

text:
Yes to both.

**It's configurable** (requirements 30–31). The audit runs only when an `audit:` key is set, either in the project's `rpir/config.yaml` or in your user config, and the project wins. Leave it unset and there's no audit, so kentra-rpir doesn't depend on ponytail. Your setup would be:

```yaml
audit:
  skill: ponytail:ponytail-audit
  args: "Audit only the files changed in {{base}}..{{head}} in {{worktree}}."
```

**ponytail-audit doesn't have `disable-model-invocation`.** Its frontmatter (ponytail 5.3.3) has only `name` and `description`. The research spike also ran it from a background subagent and got its report back. The refusal in requirement 30 is only a guard for other skills someone might configure: a skill marked that way can't be run by an agent at all. Without the guard, the audit would fail silently.

One thing to know: ponytail-audit is written to audit the whole repo. `args` is how you narrow it to the change's diff, as in the example. Without it, you'd get findings about code the change never touched, and review would judge and apply those too.
